risk_if_not_implemented: Without Safety Instrumented System (SIS), Operational Technology (OT) and embedded systems may fail unsafely or be manipulated, endangering personnel, physical assets and process availability. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), OT Safety / Process Availability Failure (R-OT-1), Injury / Loss of Life (R-SF-1), Physical / Environmental Damage (R-SF-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack (MT-30).

compensating_control_1.name: Safe Operations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to continuously validate autonomous systems that trigger an automatic state change when safe operation is no longer assured.
compensating_control_1.justification: Safe Operations (EMB-23) provides safety assurance that compensates for the absence of Safety Instrumented System (SIS) (EMB-25) by providing alternative safety controls that reduce the likelihood and impact of unsafe conditions. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Safety Assessment
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to evaluate the safety aspects of embedded technologies via a fault tree analysis, or similar method, to determine possible consequences of misuse, misconfiguration and/or failure.
compensating_control_2.justification: Safety Assessment (EMB-19) provides periodic assessment and verification that compensates for the absence of Safety Instrumented System (SIS) (EMB-25) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
